Q1Physics
subjectPhysics
chapterElectrostatics high confidence
why this chapterThe answer turns on the potential being constant everywhere inside and on a charged thin spherical shell (equipotential volume of a conductor), so the potential difference between centre C and surface point P is zero.
subtopic 1Potential Due to Linear and Surface Charge Distribution
why this subtopicThe answer (zero) depends on the potential due to a uniformly charged thin spherical shell being constant everywhere inside and equal to its surface value kq/R, so the centre C and surface point P are at the same potential.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A thin spherical shell is charged by some source. The potential difference between the two points C and P (in V) shown in the figure is: (Take 14πε0 = 9 × 109 SI units)
  1. 3 × 105
  2. 1 × 105
  3. 0.5 × 105
  4. Zero
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (4)
  1. For uniformly charged spherical shell,
  2. V = kqR (For r ≤ R)
  3. ∴ VC = VP
  4. VC - VP = Zero

→ the working concludes: option 4

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 4 · high
  1. For a thin charged spherical shell, E = 0 for r < R.
  2. So the potential is constant inside and equals the surface value: VC = Vsurface = kqR.
  3. Point P lies on the shell, so VP = kqR = 9 × 109 × 10-60.03 = 3 × 105 V.
  4. VC - VP = 3 × 105 - 3 × 105 = 0, which is option 4.

Q2Physics
subjectPhysics
chapterSemiconductor Electronics high confidence
why this chapterThe answer depends on working out the logic gate combination's truth table and seeing it matches an AND gate, which is taught under Logic Gates in Semiconductor Electronics.
subtopic 1Logic Gates
why this subtopicThe answer depends on reducing a combination of NAND (as NOT), NOR (as NOT) and NOR gates to an equivalent AND gate, which is logic gate theory.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
The output (Y) of the given logic gate is similar to the output of an/a
  1. NAND gate
  2. NOR gate
  3. OR gate
  4. AND gate
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (4)
  1. Y1 = A · A = A
  2. Y2 = B + B = B
  3. Y = Y1 + Y2
  4. = A + B = A · B
  5. = A.B is similar to output of AND Gate

→ the working concludes: option 4

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 4 · high
  1. The top NAND gate has both inputs joined to A, so its output is A · A = A.
  2. The bottom NOR gate has both inputs joined to B, so its output is B + B = B.
  3. The final NOR gate gives Y = A + B.
  4. By De Morgan's theorem, A + B = A · B.
  5. Y = A · B is the AND gate output, which is option 4.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict

stepsRecognise the NAND gate with both inputs tied to A acts as a NOT gate, giving A-bar → Recognise the NOR gate with both inputs tied to B acts as a NOT gate, giving B-bar → Feed A-bar and B-bar into the final NOR gate and simplify (A-bar + B-bar)-bar by De Morgan's theorem to identify the equivalent single gate
whyThe work is reducing two shorted-input gates to inverters and then applying De Morgan's theorem to the NOR of the inverted inputs to name the equivalent gate.

Q3Physics
subjectPhysics
chapterWave Optics high confidence
why this chapterThe answer turns on the fringe pattern in Young's double-slit experiment with white light (zero path difference gives a central white fringe with coloured fringes around it), which is wave optics.
subtopic 1Young's Double-Slit Experiment (YDSE)
why this subtopicThe answer depends on the fringe pattern Young's double-slit experiment gives with white light: a central bright white fringe with a few coloured fringes around it.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
If the monochromatic source in Young’s double slit experiment is replaced by white light, then
  1. Interference pattern will disappear
  2. There will be a central dark fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes
  3. There will be a central bright white fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes
  4. All bright fringes will be of equal width
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (3)
  1. At central point on screen, path difference is zero for all wavelength.
  2. So, central bright fringe is white and other fringes depend on wavelength as β = λ Dd.
  3. Therefore, other fringes will be coloured.

→ the working concludes: option 3

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 3 · high
  1. At the central point the path difference is Δ = 0 for every wavelength, so every colour has a maximum there and the central fringe is bright white.
  2. Fringe width β = λ Dd depends on λ, so the bright fringes of different colours do not coincide away from the centre and the nearby fringes are coloured (blue nearest, red farther).
  3. After a few fringes the colours overlap so much that the pattern washes out, so there is a central bright white fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes, which is option 3.

subjectPhysics
chapterUnits and Measurements high confidence
why this chapterThe answer turns on the vernier constant (least count) of a vernier callipers, 1 MSD - 1 VSD = MSD/(N+1), which is taught under Vernier Calliper and Screw Gauge in Units and Measurements.
subtopic 1Vernier Calliper and Screw Gauge
why this subtopicThe answer depends on the vernier constant of a vernier calliper, VC = 1 MSD - 1 VSD = MSD/(N+1), which is taught under the vernier calliper.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
In a vernier callipers, (N+1) divisions of vernier scale coincide with N divisions of main scale. If 1 MSD represents 0.1 mm, the vernier constant (in cm) is:
  1. 110N
  2. 1100(N+1)
  3. 100N
  4. 10(N+1)
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (2)
  1. V.C = MSD - VSD ...(1)
  2. given : (N + 1) VSD = N MSD
  3. VSD = (NN+1)MSD ...(2)
  4. From (1) and (2)
  5. V.C = (MSD) - NN+1(MSD)
  6. = MSD(1 - NN+1) = MSDN+1
  7. = 0.01N+1 = 1100(N+1)

→ the working concludes: option 2

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 2 · high
  1. (N+1) VSD = N MSD, so 1 VSD = NN+1 MSD.
  2. VC = 1 MSD - 1 VSD = (1 - NN+1)MSD = 1N+1 MSD.
  3. 1 MSD = 0.1 mm = 0.01 cm = 1100 cm.
  4. VC = 1100(N+1) cm, which is option 2.

ConceptThe vernier constant is one main-scale division minus one vernier division, which equals 1 MSD divided by the number of vernier divisions
Why this answerThis question requires the least count built from the printed coincidence and then converted to centimetres, demonstrated by the stem's '(N+1) divisions of vernier scale coincide with N divisions of main scale' together with its demand for 'the vernier constant (in cm)'.
What catches a student
The trapoption 1Formula misusedformula_misusedthe right formula with a wrong power, a dropped term or the wrong quantity

Carrying the familiar least count = 1 MSDN instead of building it from the printed coincidence puts N under the 0.1, and leaving that 0.1 in millimetres while the answer is wanted in centimetres prints the result as 110N.

Who fallsa student who has memorised least count = 1 MSDN from the usual vernier, where N vernier divisions span N-1 main divisions

Why it feels rightN is the letter the stem puts on the scale and 0.1 is the number beside it, so 0.1N comes out in the same reciprocal form the options are written in

  1. badLeast count = 1 MSDN = 0.1N.Here (N+1) vernier divisions span N main divisions, so one vernier division is NN+1 MSD and the constant is 1 MSDN+1.
  2. badRead 0.1N as centimetres because the answer is wanted in cm, giving 110N.0.1 mm is 0.01 cm, so the denominator carries 100, not 10.
No route to itoption 3

Worked the two wrong turns this question offers: dividing by N instead of N+1 gives 1100N cm, and leaving the 0.1 in millimetres gives 110(N+1) cm. 100N is the reciprocal of the first of those, and no step in 1 MSD - 1 VSD inverts the result; 100N cm also exceeds one main-scale division for every N ≥ 1, which a vernier constant cannot do.

No route to itoption 4

Same two wrong turns checked against 10(N+1): it is the reciprocal of 110(N+1), the unit-slip value, and subtracting one vernier division from one main-scale division produces no reciprocal at any stage; like option 3 it is larger than one main-scale division for every N ≥ 1.

READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A light ray enters through a right angled prism at point P with the angle of incidence 30° as shown in figure. It travels through the prism parallel to its base BC and emerges along the face AC. The refractive index of the prism is:
  1. 54
  2. 52
  3. 34
  4. 32
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (2)
  1. A = 90°
  2. In prism, r1 + c = A
  3. r1 = 90° - c    …(1)
  4. sin c = 1μ ⇒ cos c = μ2 - 1μ
  5. ⇒ Apply Snell's law, on incidence surface
  6. 1 · sin 30° = μ sin(r1) ⇒ 1 × 12 = μ × sin(90° - c)
  7. 12 = μ × μ2 - 1μ
  8. On squaring 14 = μ2 - 1
  9. ⇒ μ2 = 54 ⇒ μ = 52

→ the working concludes: option 2

printed solution, as in the booklet

  1. From the figure the prism angle is A = 90°, so the refraction angles inside satisfy r1 + r2 = A = 90°.
  2. Snell's law at face AB: sin 30° = μ sin r1 ⇒ sin r1 = 12μ.
  3. The ray emerges along face AC (grazing emergence), so μ sin r2 = sin 90° = 1 ⇒ sin r2 = 1μ.
  4. Since r2 = 90° - r1, cos r1 = 1μ.
  5. sin2 r1 + cos2 r1 = 1 ⇒ 14μ2 + 1μ2 = 54μ2 = 1.
  6. μ = 52, which is option 2.

stepsApply Snell's law at P on face AB: sin 30 deg = μ sin r1 → Read 'emerges along the face AC' as grazing emergence, so the angle of incidence inside at AC is the critical angle: μ sin r2 = 1 → Use the prism geometry r1 + r2 = A with A = 90 deg, so sin r2 = cos r1 and μ cos r1 = 1 → Eliminate r1 by squaring and adding (sin2 r1 + cos2 r1 = 1) to get μ2 = 1/4 + 1 and take the root

the catchThe candidate must translate 'emerges along the face AC' into the critical-angle condition and spot that the right angle at A turns sin r2 into cos r1; the 'parallel to base' detail is a distraction that does not by itself fix r1.

printed in the booklet

In the above diagram, a strong bar magnet is moving towards solenoid-2 from solenoid-1. The direction of induced current in solenoid-1 and that in solenoid-2, respectively, are through the directions:
  1. AB and DC
  2. BA and CD
  3. AB and CD
  4. BA and DC
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (1)
  1. North of magnet is moving away from solenoid 1 so end B of solenoid 1 is South and as south of magnet is approaching solenoid 2 so end C of solenoid 2 is South.

→ the working concludes: unclear

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 1 · medium
  1. The magnet has N on the left (facing solenoid-1) and S on the right (facing solenoid-2), and it moves to the right with velocity v.
  2. Solenoid-1: the N pole moves away, so by Lenz's law the flux decrease is opposed and the near (right) face of solenoid-1 becomes an S pole to attract it.
  3. An S face means the induced current is clockwise as seen from the magnet; with the wire rising on the front strokes from A, this is current from A to B.
  4. Solenoid-2: the S pole approaches, so the near (left) face of solenoid-2 becomes an S pole to repel it, i.e. current clockwise as seen from the magnet.
  5. Solenoid-2 is viewed from the opposite side but wound the same way, so the current runs from the right lead to the left lead: D → C.
  6. Induced currents are AB and DC, which is option 1.

  2. B. If sheet is non-magnetic, no force needed.

  1. A magnetic sheet is attracted towards the strong pole, so a force is needed to hold it in place: A is true.
  2. A non-magnetic sheet at rest feels no magnetic force, so no force is needed to hold it: B is false.
  3. When a conducting sheet moves away from the pole, the flux through it changes, inducing eddy currents that by Lenz's law oppose the motion; a force F = Feddy is needed to keep v uniform: C is true.
  4. A non-conducting, non-polar sheet has no induced currents and no magnetic interaction, so with uniform velocity ∑ F = 0 needs no applied force: D is false.

publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
1 gram of sodium hydroxide was treated with 25 mL of 0.75 M HCl solution, the mass of sodium hydroxide left unreacted is equal to
  1. 750 mg
  2. 250 mg
  3. Zero mg
  4. 200 mg
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (2)
  1. M = W × 1000M2 × V (in mL)
  2. W = M × M2 × V (in mL)1000 = 0.75 × 36.5 × 251000
  3. = 0.684 g (Mass of HCl)
  4. 36.5 gHCl + 40 gNaOH ⟶ HCl + NaOH
  5. 36.5 g HCl reacts with NaOH = 40 g
  6. 0.684 g HCl reacts with NaOH = 4036.5 × 0.684 ≃ 0.750 g
  7. Amount of NaOH left = 1 g - 0.750 g = 0.250 g = 250 mg

→ the working concludes: option 2

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 2 · high
  1. Moles of NaOH: nNaOH = 1 g40 g mol-1 = 0.025 mol.
  2. Moles of HCl: nHCl = 0.025 L × 0.75 mol L-1 = 0.01875 mol.
  3. NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O is 1:1, so 0.01875 mol NaOH reacts.
  4. Unreacted NaOH: 0.025 - 0.01875 = 0.00625 mol.
  5. Mass left: 0.00625 × 40 = 0.25 g = 250 mg, which is option 2.

  1. Across period 2, Δi H1 generally increases with nuclear charge, so Li is lowest and N is highest.

      Which one of the following can be explained on the basis of Mendel's Law of Dominance? Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

      The publisher's solutionprinted answer (2)
      1. According to Law of Dominance
      2. (1) Characters are controlled by discrete units called factors
      3. (2) Factors occur in pairs
      4. (3) In a dissimilar pair of factors one member of the pair dominates (dominant) the other recessive
      5. The law of dominance is used to explain the expression of only one of the parental characters in a monohybrid cross.
      6. Law of segregation is based on the fact that the alleles do not show any expression and both the characters are recovered as such in F2 generation

      → the working concludes: option 2

      printed solution, as in the booklet
      Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 2 · high
      1. NCERT states the Law of Dominance as: characters are controlled by discrete units called factors; factors occur in pairs; in a dissimilar pair one factor dominates the other.
      2. So D (discrete unit called factor) and C (factors occur in pairs) are part of the law.
      3. A (one factor of a pair is dominant, the other recessive) is the core of the law.
      4. E: the law explains why only one of the parental characters is expressed in the F1 of a monohybrid cross, so E is explained.
      5. B is wrong: alleles do show expression, and the statement does not follow from dominance.
      6. Correct set is A, C, D and E only, which is option 2.

      2. Energy reaching the second trophic level = 0.1 × 100x = 10x (kcal m-2) yr-1.
      3. Energy reaching the third trophic level = 0.1 × 10x = x (kcal m-2) yr-1, which is option 2.

      printed in the booklet
      publisher’s solution, as printed
      READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
      Identify the step in tricarboxylic acid cycle, which does not involve oxidation of substrate.
      1. Malic acid → Oxaloacetic acid
      2. Succinic acid → Malic acid
      3. Succinyl-CoA → Succinic acid
      4. Isocitrate → α-ketoglutaric acid
      The publisher's solutionprinted answer (3)
      1. Oxidation involves the loss of electrons (often as part of hydrogen) from a molecule, leaving to an increase in its oxidation state.
      2. This process is typically associated with the transfer of electrons to an electron acceptor which is reduced in the process.
      3. The conversion of succinyl CoA to succinic acid does not involve oxidation of substrate.

      → the working concludes: option 3

      printed solution, as in the booklet
      Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 3 · high
      1. Malic acid → oxaloacetic acid is a dehydrogenation: NAD+ → NADH + H+, so the substrate is oxidised.
      2. Succinic acid → malic acid passes through fumarate; succinate → fumarate reduces FAD → FADH2, so it involves oxidation.
      3. Isocitrate → α-ketoglutaric acid is oxidative decarboxylation: NAD+ → NADH + H+ and CO2 released.
      4. Succinyl-CoA → succinic acid releases CoA and forms GTP (or ATP) by substrate-level phosphorylation, with no electron carrier reduced.
      5. So the step without substrate oxidation is option 3.

      READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
      Regarding catalytic cycle of an enzyme action, select the correct sequential steps : Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
      ASubstrate enzyme complex formation.
      BFree enzyme ready to bind with another substrate.
      CRelease of products.
      DChemical bonds of the substrate broken.
      ESubstrate binding to active site.

      4. E, D, C, B, A
      The publisher's solutionprinted answer (1)
      1. The correct answer is option (1) which is E, A, D, C, B.
      2. The catalytic cycle of an enzyme action can be described in the following steps.
      3. (1) First, the substrate binds to the active site of the enzyme, fitting into the active site.
      4. (2) The binding of the substrate induces the enzyme to alter its shape, fitting more tightly around the substrate.
      5. (3) The active site of the enzyme, now in close proximity of the substrate breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate and the new enzyme-product complex is formed.
      6. (4) The enzyme releases the products of the reaction and the free enzyme is ready to bind to another molecule of the substrate and run through the catalytic cycle once again.
      7. Options (2), (3) and (4) are incorrect as the steps mentioned are in the wrong sequence.

      → the working concludes: option 1

      printed solution, as in the booklet
      Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 1 · high
      1. The substrate first binds to the active site of the enzyme: step E.
      2. Binding induces the enzyme to alter its shape, forming the enzyme-substrate complex: step A.
      3. The active site, now close to the substrate, breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate, forming the enzyme-product complex: step D.
      4. The enzyme releases the products of the reaction: step C.
      5. The free enzyme is ready to bind another substrate and run the cycle again: step B.
      6. Sequence E, A, D, C, B matches option 1.

      Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 1 · high
      1. GnRH from the hypothalamus stimulates the pituitary to release two gonadotropins, LH and FSH, so the right-hand branch (A) = FSH.
      2. LH acts on the Leydig (interstitial) cells, which secrete androgens, so (B) = Leydig cells.
      3. FSH acts on the Sertoli cells, which secrete factors that help spermatogenesis, so (C) = Sertoli cells.
      4. Androgens drive the formation of spermatids; the Sertoli-cell factors then aid the conversion of spermatids to sperms, so (D) = spermiogenesis.
      5. The sequence FSH, Leydig cells, Sertoli cells, spermiogenesis is option 1.
